member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.BiDiDriver
member.summary: Object containing commands to drive a browser using the WebDriver BiDi protocol.

remarks.para:
Thread Safety: This class is thread-safe for concurrent command execution.
and module command methods may be called concurrently from multiple threads. Configuration operations (, , ) must complete before is called and are serialized via an internal lock.

Interface Design: This class implements three focused interfaces (, , ) for advanced framework, testing, and extensibility scenarios. Most application code should use directly and ignore these interfaces. See the Core Concepts documentation for guidance on when each interface applies.

remarks.para:
This constructor is used when you need to provide a custom instance, typically for advanced scenarios such as:
Using a custom implementation with specific timeout configurations
Sharing a transport across multiple driver instances (not recommended for typical usage)
Integrating with specialized connection management frameworks

Ownership: a driver takes ownership of the transport passed to it. disposes the transport, which in turn disposes its . A transport shared between drivers is therefore torn down for every one of them as soon as the first is disposed, so a shared transport must outlive all of its drivers, or the drivers must not be disposed.
Most users should use the simpler constructor instead, which creates a default WebSocket-based transport automatically.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.BiDiDriver.IsStarted
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the driver has started communication with the remote end of the WebDriver BiDi protocol.

remarks.para: This property returns after completes successfully and remains until is called or the connection is lost.

The value reflects the state the transport itself tracks across its own connect and disconnect operations; it is not a live query of the underlying . The two can therefore disagree briefly: a connection that reaches end-of-file, for example, reports itself inactive before the transport's disconnection handling has run and cleared this value.
Use this property to check driver state before executing commands or during cleanup operations.

Important timing restriction: Modules (), custom events (), and type info resolvers () must be registered before calling ; attempting any of these after the driver has started throws an . Adding observers to an with is not restricted and may be done at any time, before or after the driver has started.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.BiDiDriver.EventHandlerExceptionBehavior
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating the behavior for handling exceptions thrown by event handlers invoked by this driver. Defaults to , meaning that exceptions from event handlers will be caught and logged but will not cause the driver to stop processing messages from the transport. Exceptions from handlers registered with participate in this behavior when they are not already owned by task capture. If the caller captures handler tasks using , , or , those task exceptions remain owned by the caller rather than being surfaced again through the transport error pipeline. This applies to handler tasks that fault asynchronously (they were still running when the handler returned). A handler task that is already faulted when the handler returns — a synchronous failure, such as a task from or an async handler that throws before its first await — is both captured and re-surfaced through the transport error pipeline.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.BiDiDriver.ProtocolErrorBehavior
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating the behavior for handling exceptions when a protocol error is received from the remote end. Defaults to , meaning that exceptions from protocol errors will be caught and logged but will not cause the driver to stop processing messages from the transport.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.BiDiDriver.UnknownMessageBehavior
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating the behavior for handling exceptions when an unknown message is encountered, such as valid JSON that does not match any protocol data structure. Defaults to , meaning that exceptions from unknown messages will be caught and logged, but will not cause the driver to stop processing messages from the transport. A response that arrives for a command after that command has timed out or been canceled is not an unknown message; it is logged and discarded without affecting this behavior.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.BiDiDriver.UnexpectedErrorBehavior
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating the behavior for handling exceptions when an unexpected error is encountered, such as an error response received with no corresponding command. Defaults to , meaning that exceptions from unexpected errors will be caught and logged but will not cause the driver to stop processing messages from the transport. An error response that arrives for a command after that command has timed out or been canceled is not an unexpected error; it is logged and discarded without affecting this behavior.

member.summary: Registers a module for use with this driver.
member.param: The module object.
member.exception: Thrown when attempting to register a module with a name that has already been registered.
Thrown when the module argument is .

remarks.para: Critical timing restriction: Modules must be registered before calling . Once the driver has started, module registration is locked to prevent race conditions with event handling.

Thread safety: This method is thread-safe and can be safely called from multiple threads concurrently. An internal lock ensures that the check against and the module addition to the registry are performed atomically, preventing race conditions during concurrent registration attempts or when registering near the time of calling .

This method is used for registering custom modules that extend the WebDriver BiDi protocol. All standard modules (Browser, BrowsingContext, Script, Network, etc.) are registered automatically during driver construction and do not need explicit registration.

member.summary: Gets a sentinel value for the property that signals the remote end to reset the viewport to its default dimensions. Assign this to the property; do not use it as a command-level reset.

remarks.para: This is a property-level sentinel, not a command-level reset. It must be assigned to the property of a instance:

When serialized, the sentinel causes the viewport field to be written as JSON null, instructing the remote end to restore the default viewport. Assigning a C# to omits the field entirely, leaving the current viewport unchanged.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.BrowsingContext.SetViewportCommandParameters.ResetToDefaultDevicePixelRatio
member.summary: Gets a sentinel value for the property that signals the remote end to reset the device pixel ratio to its default value. Assign this to the property; do not use it as a command-level reset.

remarks.para: This is a property-level sentinel, not a command-level reset. It must be assigned to the property of a instance:

When serialized, the sentinel (any negative value) causes the devicePixelRatio field to be written as JSON null, instructing the remote end to restore the default pixel ratio. Assigning a C# to omits the field entirely, leaving the current pixel ratio unchanged.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.CommandParameters.AdditionalData
member.summary: Gets additional properties to be serialized with this command.

remarks.para: The WebDriver BiDi protocol allows for additional command properties that are not defined in the specification. This dictionary allows users to include those additional properties while maintaining the strongly-typed nature of the CommandParameters class. The entries in this dictionary are intentionally mutable, so that users can add additional properties as needed.

Entries are serialized as additional properties inside the params object of the command message, alongside the typed parameter properties. They are not written at the envelope level next to id, method, and params; for envelope-level properties, override and populate .

Though the values of this dictionary are typed as , they will be serialized to JSON using the same rules as other properties of the command. This means that values can be of any type that is serializable to JSON, including complex objects, arrays, and primitive types. However, custom types should be designed with JSON serialization in mind to ensure they are serialized correctly, including use of the appropriate attributes for JSON serialization by .

AOT / trimming note: because the entries are typed as , serialization of their runtime types relies on reflection-based overloads that are not compatible with trimming or native AOT. Consumers that publish with PublishAot=true and use this dictionary must ensure every value's runtime type is discoverable by a registered (see ), or the command will fail at send time with a .

member.summary: A data class representing a set of geolocation coordinates.

member.name: M:WebDriverBiDi.Emulation.GeolocationCoordinates.#ctor(System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: The latitude of the geographic position in degrees. Positive values are north of the equator; negative values are south of the equator.
The longitude of the geographic position in degrees. Positive values are east of the prime meridian; negative values are west of the prime meridian.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Emulation.GeolocationCoordinates.Latitude
member.summary: Gets or sets the latitude of the geographic position in degrees. Positive values are north of the equator; negative values are south of the equator.
member.remarks: Valid values for this property range from -90.0 to 90.0, inclusive. This property does not validate its value; a value outside this range is sent as-is, and a conforming remote end rejects it when the command is executed.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Emulation.GeolocationCoordinates.Longitude
member.summary: Gets or sets the longitude of the geographic position in degrees. Positive values are east of the prime meridian; negative values are west of the prime meridian.
member.remarks: Valid values for this property range from -180.0 to 180.0, inclusive. This property does not validate its value; a value outside this range is sent as-is, and a conforming remote end rejects it when the command is executed.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Emulation.GeolocationCoordinates.Accuracy
member.summary: Gets or sets the accuracy of the geographic position to a 95% confidence level. If omitted, is interpreted as 1.0.
member.remarks: Valid values for this property are greater than or equal to 0.0. This property does not validate its value; a value outside this range is sent as-is, and a conforming remote end rejects it when the command is executed.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Emulation.GeolocationCoordinates.Altitude
member.summary: Gets or sets the altitude of the geographic position, in meters.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Emulation.GeolocationCoordinates.AltitudeAccuracy
member.summary: Gets or sets the accuracy of the altitude of the geographic position to a 95% confidence level.
member.remarks: Valid values for this property are greater than or equal to 0.0. This property does not validate its value; a value outside this range is sent as-is, and a conforming remote end rejects it when the command is executed.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Emulation.GeolocationCoordinates.Heading
member.summary: Gets or sets the heading of the movement of the geographic position, in degrees. If the device is stationary, leave this property unset ().
member.remarks: Valid values for this property range from 0.0 inclusive to 360.0 exclusive: the specification's CDDL range 0.0...360.0 excludes its upper bound, so 360.0 itself is not a valid heading (use 0.0). This property does not validate its value; a value outside this range is sent as-is, and a conforming remote end rejects it when the command is executed.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Emulation.GeolocationCoordinates.Speed
member.summary: Gets or sets the speed of the movement of the geographic position, in meters per second. If the device is stationary, should be set to 0.
member.remarks: Valid values for this property are greater than or equal to 0.0. This property does not validate its value; a value outside this range is sent as-is, and a conforming remote end rejects it when the command is executed.

member.summary: Enumeration of error codes that may be returned by the remote end of the WebDriver BiDi protocol in error responses to commands or in unsolicited error events. Each value corresponds to a specific error type defined in the WebDriver BiDi protocol specification, and is associated with a specific string value used in the JSON error responses.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.EventDataCollector`1
member.summary: Specialized observer of an event that collects event data each time the event is raised, for on-demand batch inspection or async streaming rather than immediate per-event reaction.
member.typeparam: The type of event arguments containing information about the observable event.

remarks.para: Use when you want to accumulate event data and examine it at a convenient point in your code. Use to drain all events that have accumulated since the last call; the internal buffer is cleared on each drain so subsequent calls return only new events. Use to stream events one at a time via ; the sequence ends when the collector is disposed.
The collector counts as one observer against the event's . Create it through and dispose it (or await using it) when collection is no longer needed to avoid memory leaks.
Thread Safety: All public members are thread-safe. and may be called concurrently with event notifications. Do not call concurrently with ; use one reading approach at a time.

member.summary: Implementation of an observer in the Observer pattern for events.
member.typeparam: The type of event arguments containing information about the observable event.

remarks.para: Capture methods (, , , , and ) are thread-safe. Only one capture session may be active at a time per observer.

Disposal: and remove the observer from its event and end any active capture session. Capture methods called afterwards throw , and a or call that is still waiting when the observer is disposed completes with rather than waiting for its timeout. , and repeated disposal remain safe no-ops.

Typical capture flow: Call before triggering the action that produces events, then use to wait for a specific number of handler tasks, or to wait for handler tasks to complete, or to collect whatever has arrived so far. When or collects the full requested batch, the capture session ends automatically; becomes a no-op and need not be called. Call explicitly only when ending the session early (e.g., on timeout or cancellation).

member.name: M:WebDriverBiDi.EventObserver`1.StartCapturingTasks
member.summary: Begins an unbounded capture session on this observer. Every handler invocation that occurs while the capture is active produces a that can be retrieved via , , or . The session ends automatically when or collects the full requested batch; call to end the session early.
member.exception: Thrown when a capture session is already active on this observer.
Thrown when the observer has been disposed.

remarks.para: This method is thread-safe. Only one capture session may be active at a time.

Ownership of each captured transfers to the caller when it is read via or . The caller is responsible for observing the result of each task, including any exceptions, to avoid unobserved task exceptions.

One kind of invocation does not produce a captured task: a failing handler registered with . Notification awaits such a handler, so its exception propagates out of the notification to the producer instead of being captured, and a wait for a fixed number of tasks is never satisfied by it. A handler registered with is captured whether it later succeeds or fails, provided it returns a task (including a task that is already faulted). A handler that instead throws synchronously, before returning a task — for example a non-async delegate that throws while producing its — propagates the exception to the producer before capture can occur, so like the synchronous-handler case it produces no captured task and never satisfies a fixed-count wait.

member.name: M:WebDriverBiDi.EventObserver`1.StopCapturingTasks
member.summary: Ends the active capture session. Any tasks still in the capture buffer can no longer be retrieved via or after this call.

remarks.para: This method is thread-safe and is idempotent: calling it when no capture is active does nothing.

If captured tasks that have not yet been retrieved may fault, call before calling this method to transfer ownership to the caller. A fault in an unretrieved, still-buffered task is always observed (no is ever raised), but it is not reported through the observer-error pipeline either — it is silently dropped, so retrieving the tasks first is the only way to see such failures.

member.name: M:WebDriverBiDi.EventObserver`1.WaitForCapturedTasksAsync(System.UInt32,System.TimeSpan,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Asynchronously waits until the specified number of handler tasks have been captured, then returns them. Ownership of the returned tasks transfers to the caller.
member.param: The number of handler tasks to wait for. Must be at least 1.
How long to wait before giving up. Must be non-negative and no greater than the maximum timer duration supported by the runtime, or to wait indefinitely.
A that can be used to cancel the wait.

returns.para: An array of captured handler objects. The length of the returned array indicates whether the wait was fulfilled:

item.description: If the array length equals , the wait was fulfilled — all expected handler invocations were captured before the timeout expired. When this is the only wait active on the observer, the capture session is automatically ended and a subsequent call is a no-op; when another wait is concurrently active, the session is left open for that waiter to continue receiving tasks.

If the array length is less than , the wait timed out — only the tasks that arrived before the timeout are returned. The capture session remains active and subsequent calls will continue collecting tasks.

member.exception: Thrown when is zero, or when is negative (other than ) or exceeds the maximum supported timer duration.
Thrown when no capture session is active.
Thrown when the observer has been disposed, or is disposed while this method is waiting.
Thrown when is cancelled.

member.name: M:WebDriverBiDi.EventObserver`1.WaitForCapturedTasksCompleteAsync(System.UInt32,System.TimeSpan,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Asynchronously waits until the specified number of handler tasks have been captured and all of them have completed execution. This method discards the tasks after completion. If you need to inspect the tasks, use either or instead. Exceptions from captured handler tasks remain owned by the caller and are propagated by this method through the returned task rather than being re-surfaced through transport-level event handler error behavior.
member.param: The number of handler tasks to wait for. Must be at least 1.

How long to wait for the handler tasks to be captured and for the handlers to complete their execution. Must be non-negative and no greater than the maximum timer duration supported by the runtime, or to wait indefinitely for both phases.
A that can be used to cancel the wait.
member.returns: if the expected number of handler tasks were captured and completed before the timeout expired; otherwise, . When is returned and no other wait is concurrently active on the observer, the capture session is automatically ended and a subsequent call is a no-op.
member.exception: Thrown when is zero, or when is negative (other than ) or exceeds the maximum supported timer duration.
Thrown when no capture session is active.
Thrown when the observer has been disposed, or is disposed while this method is waiting.
Thrown when is cancelled.

remarks.para: A return can arise from two distinct timeout conditions:

item.description: Fewer than events arrived before the timeout expired (the capture phase timed out). The capture session remains active; subsequent handler invocations continue to be buffered.

All events arrived but one or more handlers had not finished executing before the remaining timeout budget was exhausted (the completion phase timed out). The capture session is automatically ended in this case, and a handler fault occurring after the timeout is observed and discarded rather than surfacing as .

remarks.para: If you need to distinguish between these two conditions, use to obtain the handler tasks and then await with your own timeout handling.

member.name: M:WebDriverBiDi.EventObserver`1.GetCapturedTasks
member.summary: Synchronously gets all tasks currently available in the capture buffer and returns them. Does not wait for additional tasks to arrive. Ownership of the returned tasks transfers to the caller.
member.returns: All handler tasks available in the capture buffer at the time of the call, or an empty array if no capture session is active.
member.exception: Thrown when the observer has been disposed.

remarks.para: This method acquires an internal reader lock that is shared with and . If a concurrent call to either of those methods holds the lock, this method will block the calling thread until that call releases it. In async contexts — particularly those with a single-threaded , such as WPF or legacy ASP.NET — prefer to avoid blocking the calling thread.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.JsonConverters.ExpandedYearDateTimeJsonConverter
member.summary: A converter to read DateTime values serialized in the ECMAScript Date.prototype.toISOString() format, including its expanded-year forms.
member.remarks: The WebDriver BiDi protocol serializes JavaScript Date objects using the format of Date.prototype.toISOString(). JavaScript dates cover approximately the years -271821 to +275760; for years outside 0000-9999 that format uses a sign and a six-digit year (for example, "+275760-09-13T00:00:00.000Z"), and year zero itself is written as "0000". None of those forms is representable by , whose range is years 0001-9999, so a structurally valid date string for an instant before that range deserializes as and one for an instant after it as , consistent with how the library clamps out-of-range protocol timestamps elsewhere. A structurally invalid date string is still rejected with a .

member.summary: Gets or sets the headers of the request.

remarks.para: This is one of the few list properties on a type that is nullable and settable, because the protocol gives a present-but-empty array its own meaning. The remote end steps for network.continueRequest state: "If command parameters contains "headers": Let headers be an empty header list" and then append each entry, so sending [] replaces the header list with none, while omitting the field keeps the original header list.
When , the property is not included in the command; when an empty list, an empty array is sent to the remote end. Every other list property is read-only and is omitted while empty.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.ObservableEventHandlerOptions
member.summary: Enumerated value describing options for the execution of a handler for an ObservableEvent.

member.name: F:WebDriverBiDi.ObservableEventHandlerOptions.RunHandlerSynchronously
member.summary: No options, meaning handlers attempt to run synchronously, awaiting the completion of execution. This is the default.

member.name: F:WebDriverBiDi.ObservableEventHandlerOptions.RunHandlerAsynchronously
member.summary: The handler's completion is not awaited by the event dispatcher. Order of multiple executions of the handler is not guaranteed.

remarks.para: This option changes what the dispatcher does with the a handler returns, not where the handler starts executing. Every handler is invoked on the thread that is dispatching the event (the transport's message-processing thread for driver events). For a Func<T, Task> handler, the code that runs before the handler returns its — in an async lambda, everything up to the first await that does not complete synchronously — still runs on the dispatching thread; only the remainder is detached. Blocking calls placed before that first await, or a non-async Task-returning handler that does its work synchronously and returns a completed task, block the dispatcher regardless of this option.
Handlers added with the Action<T> overload of AddObserver are the exception: with this option the whole action is queued to the thread pool, so none of it runs on the dispatching thread.

To offload blocking work from a Task-returning handler, make it async and place an await (for example await Task.Yield()) before the blocking work, or wrap the work in Task.Run. The BIDI007 and BIDI023 analyzers report handlers where this option cannot help.

remarks.para: This class is public to support AOT (ahead-of-time) compilation scenarios in extension libraries. End users do not construct or reference this type directly; it is used internally by to express the expected response type for a command.

Authors of third-party extension libraries that add new protocol commands must not register this envelope type in their own : its serializable members are internal to this library, so a context in another assembly cannot generate working metadata for it. The transport builds the envelope's type info itself (see ) and asks the serializer options only for the result type. Annotate your context with [JsonSerializable(typeof(TResult))] for each custom result type, then register the context via . See the AOT compatibility article in the library documentation for the full pattern.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.Connection
member.summary: Represents a connection to a WebDriver Bidi remote end.

remarks.para: The class is an abstract base class that defines the contract for transport-layer communication with a browser. It is wrapped by the class, which handles protocol-level concerns like JSON serialization and command/response correlation.
Most users will never need to interact with objects directly. The class manages connections automatically. Custom connection implementations are only needed for specialized transport mechanisms.

Available implementations:
Standard WebSocket transport (recommended for all scenarios)
Anonymous pipes transport (specialized for high-performance local Chromium automation)

Thread safety: Connection implementations use internal synchronization to ensure thread-safe operation. Multiple threads can safely call concurrently. The class that wraps connections provides additional synchronization for and operations.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.Connection.StartupTimeout
member.summary: Gets or sets the value of the timeout to wait before throwing an error when starting up the connection.
member.remarks:
The timeout is a single budget for the whole of startup: it bounds each individual connection attempt as well as the retries between them, so a remote end that accepts slowly is cut off at the deadline rather than allowed to complete late. Name resolution and address fallback (for example localhost resolving to an IPv6 address first) count against the budget, so avoid sub-second values when connecting by host name.
Because the startup budget is computed by subtracting elapsed time, it must be a finite value; is not permitted.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is negative, is , or exceeds the maximum timer duration supported by the runtime.

member.summary: Installs the reporter used to surface failures of observers of this connection's events that occur after the observer's handler has already returned to the caller.
member.param: The reporter callback.

remarks.para: A failure of that kind cannot propagate to a caller, because the handler has already returned. Without a reporter it is observed (so it never surfaces as a ) but is otherwise discarded. calls this so that such a failure is instead routed through the same unhandled-error pipeline as a failure in an observer of a transport, driver, or module event, and is therefore governed by .
The reporter applies to observers added before this call as well as after it, because reads it when a fault is reported rather than capturing it when the observer is created.

member.name: M:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.Connection.StartDataReceiveTask
member.summary: Starts the task that receives data on this connection, as defined by the implementation of .

remarks.para: This method attaches a continuation to the task on which the receive loop runs. The receive loop runs on a fire-and-forget task, and shutdown paths are not guaranteed to await it: abandons the loop when it does not finish within , and disposal skips entirely when the connection is already inactive. An abandoned task that faults would otherwise sit unobserved until the finalizer raises , which surfaces as a failure in whatever code happens to be running when the garbage collector runs.
Reading inside the continuation observes the fault and yields it for reporting. This does not prevent a shutdown path that does await the task from seeing the exception.

member.summary: Disposes and recreates the connection's , readying this connection for a new session.
member.remarks: Call this from before any operation that consumes . Because cancels the source unconditionally -- including when the connection never started -- a session that reuses the previous source would begin with cancellation already requested and could never connect.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.IPipeServerProcessProvider
member.summary: Defines an interface for providing a process that hosts a pipe server. This allows for dependency injection and testing of components that rely on a pipe server process.

remarks.para: This interface is used by to manage the browser process lifecycle when using anonymous pipes for communication. Implementations are responsible for starting the browser process with the --remote-debugging-pipe flag and providing pipe handles for communication.

The provided process must:
Be started before is called
Accept pipe handles via command-line arguments or environment variables
Support the null-terminated JSON message protocol
Read from file descriptor/handle for incoming messages
Write to file descriptor/handle for outgoing messages
Note: This interface is rarely needed by most users. Browser launchers that support pipe connections typically implement this interface internally.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.PendingCommandCollection
member.summary: Object containing a thread-safe collection of pending commands.

remarks.para: In addition to the commands that are awaiting a response, the collection remembers a bounded number of commands that were canceled while pending (see and ). The remote end does not know that the local end has stopped waiting, so it may still send a response for such a command; lets the transport recognize that response and discard it, rather than treating it as an unknown message or an unexpected error.

At most canceled commands are remembered; when the limit is exceeded, the oldest entries are forgotten first. A response for a forgotten command is treated as an unknown message, exactly as a response for a command that was never sent.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.PipeConnection
member.summary: Represents a connection to a WebDriver Bidi remote end over anonymous pipes. This is used with Chromium's --remote-debugging-pipe flag, which on non-Windows systems communicates via file descriptors 3 (browser reads) and 4 (browser writes).

remarks.para: provides a specialized transport mechanism for browser communication using anonymous pipes instead of WebSockets. This offers slightly lower latency but requires the browser and application to be on the same machine.

item.description: High-performance local test suites where latency is critical
Browser implementation supports --remote-debugging-pipe (currently only Chromium-based browsers)
Browser and tests run on the same machine
Messages are null-terminated JSON strings (each message ends with \0)
On Unix systems: Browser reads from file descriptor 3, writes to file descriptor 4
On Windows: Uses named pipe handles
Requires for process lifecycle management
Only supported by Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge)
Cannot connect to remote browsers
More complex setup than WebSocket connections

remarks.para: Recommendation: Most users should use instead. Pipe connections are only beneficial for specialized high-performance scenarios with Chromium browsers.

member.summary: Asynchronously stops communication with the remote end of this connection.
member.param: A cancellation token used to propagate notification that the operation should be canceled.
member.returns: The task object representing the asynchronous operation.
member.remarks: Waiting for the receive loop to finish is bounded by . Unlike , where cancelling the connection's token reliably aborts a pending receive, cancelling the pipe connection's token does not guarantee that an in-progress pipe read unblocks promptly on every supported target framework. If the receive loop does not finish within the timeout, a warning is logged and this method returns anyway; the receive task continues running in the background until the pipe unblocks on its own. While that abandoned loop is still running, refuses to begin a new session, and any data the abandoned read eventually returns is discarded rather than dispatched.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.Transport
member.summary: The transport object used for serializing and deserializing JSON data used in the WebDriver Bidi protocol. It uses a object to communicate with the remote end, and does no further processing of the objects serialized or deserialized. Consumers of this class are expected to handle things like awaiting the response of a WebDriver BiDi command message.

remarks.para: Message Queue Architecture: This transport uses an unbounded for message processing. Messages received from the connection are queued and processed sequentially by a dedicated reader task.

Memory Considerations: The unbounded queue means there is no limit on the number of messages that can be buffered if they arrive faster than they can be processed. In typical usage, message processing is fast enough that queue depth remains minimal. However, in high-throughput scenarios (e.g., thousands of rapid events or very slow event handlers), memory consumption could grow significantly.

Performance Characteristics: The single-reader, single-writer queue design provides optimal throughput for the typical case where messages arrive sequentially and are processed quickly. Event handlers that perform slow operations (I/O, CPU-intensive work) should use to avoid blocking the message processing thread.

Monitoring Queue Behavior: Use to monitor the number of messages buffered in the queue. A persistently growing value indicates that event handlers are not keeping up with the incoming message rate. If you suspect message backlog issues, consider:
Using for all event handlers that perform I/O or take more than a few milliseconds
Reducing the frequency of subscribed events if not all are needed
Implementing throttling or filtering logic in your event handlers

Thread Safety: This class is thread-safe. may be called concurrently from multiple threads. Connection lifecycle operations (, ) are serialized via an internal semaphore. Both and check the connected state before taking the semaphore (and again after acquiring it). This prevents a deadlock when a disconnect is triggered while another caller already holds the lock, and lets a command sent from a synchronous event handler while is in progress fail immediately with rather than blocking on the semaphore for the duration of the shutdown wait. Event observers may be added or removed concurrently with message processing.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.Transport.ShutdownTimeout
member.summary: Gets or sets the timeout to wait for message processing to complete during shutdown. If message processing does not complete within this timeout, the shutdown will proceed without waiting for the remaining processing to finish. Messages still in the queue will not be processed, and any pending commands will be canceled. The default is 10 seconds.
member.remarks: This timeout applies to waiting for the incoming message queue to empty, to waiting for the messages in the queue to be processed, and, during disposal, to waiting for an in-flight connect attempt to complete before the transport's resources are released.
member.exception: Thrown when the value is negative (other than ) or exceeds the maximum timer duration supported by the runtime.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.Transport.IncomingQueueDepth
member.summary: Gets the number of messages currently buffered in the incoming message queue and waiting to be processed by the reader task.

remarks.para: This property surfaces the depth of the unbounded described in the class-level remarks. It is intended for diagnostics and observability: a persistently growing value indicates that event handlers are not keeping up with the incoming message rate, and should prompt investigation of handler duration or the use of .

The value reflects the queue for the current connection. The counter is reset to zero on each call to alongside the channel replacement. Reading this property before has ever been called, or after , returns the depth of the remaining (possibly drained) queue rather than throwing.

Reconnect transient overcount: The reset and channel replacement occur together under the connect/disconnect semaphore, but a TryWrite call already in progress on the old channel will increment the counter after the reset. This produces a brief positive overcount (never a negative value) during reconnect. The effect is observability-only and resolves on the next message dispatch.
Thread Safety: This property is safe to read concurrently with message production and consumption. The returned value is a snapshot and may be stale by the time the caller observes it.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.Transport.PendingCommandCount
member.summary: Gets the number of commands that have been sent to the remote end and are awaiting a response.

remarks.para: This property is intended for diagnostics and observability alongside . A persistently high value suggests that the remote end is not responding promptly, or that a burst of commands is in flight without corresponding responses yet.

Reading this property before has ever been called, or after , returns the count of the pending-command collection in its current state rather than throwing. The collection is cleared during , so reads after a disconnect typically return zero.
Thread Safety: This property is safe to read concurrently with command send and response processing. The returned value is a snapshot and may be stale by the time the caller observes it.

member.name: P:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.Transport.State
member.summary: Gets a value indicating the lifecycle state of this transport with respect to its connection to a remote end. The returned value is a snapshot and may be stale by the time the caller observes it.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.Protocol.WebSocketConnection
member.summary: Represents a connection to a WebDriver Bidi remote end over a WebSocket.

remarks.para: is the standard and recommended transport mechanism for WebDriver BiDi. It uses the class to communicate with the browser over the WebSocket protocol (ws:// or wss:// schemes).

item.description: All standard automation scenarios (local or remote browsers)
Containerized browser environments
Cross-machine browser debugging
Any browser supporting WebDriver BiDi (Chrome, Edge, Firefox)
Universal browser support
Network flexibility (local and remote)
Low latency (1-3ms per message for local connections)

Automatic retry on startup (retries every 500ms within StartupTimeout; both each attempt and the pause between attempts are bounded by the remaining StartupTimeout, so neither a host that never answers nor one that refuses immediately can hold startup open past the timeout)
Supports reconnection after calling StopAsync

remarks.para: Most users will never create a directly. The creates one automatically when constructed without a custom transport.

member.summary: Asynchronously stops communication with the remote end of this connection.
member.param: A cancellation token used to propagate notification that the operation should be canceled.
member.returns: The task object representing the asynchronous operation.
member.remarks: Waiting for the receive loop to finish is bounded by . If the receive loop does not finish within the timeout, a warning is logged and this method returns anyway; the receive task continues running in the background until the receive loop unblocks on its own. Because cancelling the connection's token reliably aborts a pending WebSocket receive, this bound is reached only when the receive loop is delayed by its own message dispatch (for example, a synchronous event observer that blocks) rather than by the socket read itself.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.Script.RemoteValueDictionary
member.summary: A read-only dictionary of RemoteValue objects.
member.remarks: Keys are either values or instances. String keys are compared by value, so dictionary["name"] works as expected. keys are compared by reference: each one denotes a distinct JavaScript object, and two object keys that happen to serialize identically (for example, two functions with no handle) remain distinct entries. Look such entries up by enumerating the dictionary, or by using the very key instance obtained from ; a separately constructed, structurally equal will not match.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.SpecRangeAttribute
member.summary: Marks a command-parameter property with the numeric range the WebDriver BiDi specification defines for its value, so that Roslyn analyzers can read the range from compiled metadata as well as from source.

remarks.para: This attribute records the specification's range for documentation and tooling only. The library deliberately does not validate a property's value against this range at run time: a value the specification places outside the range is representable on the wire, and a conforming remote end rejects it when the command is executed. Bounds are inclusive of both and , unless is set to , in which case a value equal to is outside the range (the specification's CDDL expresses such a range with the ... operator rather than ..). Use or for a range that is unbounded on that side.

Some properties accept a reset sentinel value that falls outside the specification range (for example, a negative value that clears an override). Set to and to that value so tooling does not treat it as out of range.

member.name: T:WebDriverBiDi.WebDriverBiDiEventSource
member.summary: EventSource for WebDriver BiDi protocol instrumentation. This EventSource provides structured diagnostic events for monitoring, tracing, and troubleshooting WebDriver BiDi operations.

remarks.para:
This EventSource can be consumed by:
EventListener (custom in-process listeners)
ETW (Event Tracing for Windows)
EventPipe (cross-platform event collection)
dotnet-trace (CLI diagnostics tool)
OpenTelemetry (via EventSource integration)
Application Insights, Dynatrace, etc. (via bridges)

para.code: using var session = EventPipeSystem.CreateSession(new EventPipeProvider("WebDriverBiDi")); // Collect events...

member.summary: Logs the current count of in-flight asynchronous event handler tasks.

A persistently growing value indicates that asynchronous handlers are accumulating faster than they complete; this may precede memory pressure and should prompt investigation of handler duration or event rate. The counter is process-global across all instances.
